title: Fix the Assignment Instead of Comparison
description: The program should check whether a number equals 10 and print a message.
expectedBehavior: Since x starts as 5, the program should print 'x is not ten'.
actualProblem: if (x = 10) assigns 10 to x instead of comparing. The assignment expression's value (10, which is non-zero/true) makes the if always take the true branch, and as a side effect, x is now permanently changed to 10.
explanation: C allows assignment expressions inside conditions because = returns the assigned value, which silently gets treated as the condition's truth value. This is a classic bug — comparisons must use ==, not =.
